subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should OpenClaw fix this WhatsApp `inter_session` delivery-loss symptom with the narrow requester-return-path/message-tool contract from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311, or wait for the broader structured handoff contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478?
rationale: The remaining evidence supports a real source-level suppression path, but the repair changes model-facing A2A source-reply semantics and intersects the stable prompt-cache contract, so automation should not choose the product contract shape.

options.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate and require the existing message-delivery/security review concerns plus redacted source-reply proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to structured callbacks
options.body: Keep this issue open but make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478 the design owner for typed skip/no-reply or delivery-intent semantics.

options.title: Require fresh WhatsApp repro first
options.body: Keep the issue blocked on a current-main WhatsApp transcript if maintainers want live channel proof before changing A2A prompt behavior.

recommendation.title: Review the narrow return-path PR
recommendation.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the current fix candidate and require the existing message-delivery/security review concerns plus redacted source-reply proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent sessions_send routing and delivery history makes this the best available owner for the narrow source-reply contract choice.
